asks.text: What would make those feel like the same mod to you, and which sentence in the proposed root gets the relationship wrong?
asks.decision: The promise that joins the parts — ASK FIRST
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1/F2. A general lighting framework and a campaign's expressive language can coexist, but a root led entirely by either can obscure why the other belongs. Their built capabilities are already accounted for.
asks.guess: The lamps are a medium others can use; the Utinni is its richest use. I recommend that emphasis, with the neutral patterns a complete experience of their own.
asks.tree_changes: If expression leads, organise the root around who is speaking and what changes in play. If the reusable medium leads, organise it around ownership, claims and consumers. If ordinary colony beauty is equally central, give it an independent promise and scene. Every answer retains built coverage; correcting the paragraph changes dependent draft claims. No answer means root remains unapproved.

asks.text: Which scene should come first when deciding whether AtmosphericBase has understood you, and what one failure there would make you stop?
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1/F2/F3. The old catalogue recommends a handover, but I found no recorded owner flagship pick. The first scene should reveal the mod's point without hiding its unfinished parts.
asks.guess: B, with deliberately different test palettes and an honest label on the simulated ranks. I recommend A as a separate ownership demonstration and C once its machinery exists.
asks.tree_changes: The chosen scene becomes the proposed first showcase, bound only after his recorded pick. A leads with reversibility; B leads with separate presences and movement; C leads with preemption and restoration and needs explicit build dependencies. Other capabilities keep their own scenes or ordinary checks. Choosing C does not certify its implementation.

asks.text: What should an experienced player be entitled to conclude from that movement: who is demanding attention, what sort of trouble it is, where to act, or something else?
asks.decision: What a warning is allowed to tell you
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1. An unmistakably different warning is already intended. A direction that looks useful but is merely decorative would promise information the framework does not possess.
asks.guess: Identity and a recognisable warning are the common promise; a useful direction is earned only when a consumer supplies a real target. I recommend avoiding a false instruction to visit the engine.
asks.tree_changes: Identity alone gives distinct warning vocabulary without a location promise. A trouble category needs authored, distinguishable categories. A location promise needs a real consumer target and an exploration where the trouble moves but the old location remains tempting. A deliberately deceptive god needs a specifically authored deception, not arbitrary wrong pointers. Lights still cause no raid or other unrelated world effect.

asks.text: After a deed really changes who is in front, what should let you notice that this was a change of power rather than the border's ordinary wandering?
asks.decision: The moment a new god takes the front
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1. The source can reorder claims and the neighbour already owns the front decision. Neither fact settles how the player recognises the transition. A pretty moving border can conceal the event.
asks.guess: A brief, recognisable handover in the incoming presence's own motion, then ordinary contested territory resumes. I recommend exploring that against a control with the same two occupants but no change of front.
asks.tree_changes: If a distinct handover matters, add a bounded transition promise tied to the real front event. If changed territory and the occupants' usual motions suffice, require correspondence to the event without inventing another flourish. If a spoken acknowledgement carries the event, the campaign owns that acknowledgement and its witness rule. The framework still reads rank from outside; this asks no new ranking algorithm.

asks.text: What would make that old rhythm feel like a memory of A rather than A still controlling the lamp?
asks.decision: A trace of the previous occupant
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1. Scar is built, so its presence is not up for keeping. Its meaning has to survive beside both an actual moving border and a third occupant's brief intrusion.
asks.guess: B's continuing motion and peaks should make present ownership clear while A remains recognisable in the low moments. I recommend showing it beside a genuine return of A and a third-presence flicker.
asks.tree_changes: If the new occupant's motion carries ownership, require it to remain recognisable through the trace. If the surrounding border provides the explanation, stage the trace with enough territory in view and check that context. If an inspect explanation is essential, add it as a supporting readout while retaining the intended visual distinction. If he delegates the exact cue, record that delegation and compare labelled explorations. The built memory and its authored exception stay accounted for; no answer licenses a third territorial owner or interpolated colours.

asks.text: What should that pause mean to the player: someone listened, someone approved, someone is about to answer, or another meaning?
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1/F2. A local hush is built, but the witness ledger and its consumers are not. Reusing the same pause for approval and menace could turn an intended acknowledgement into a false promise.
asks.guess: It means attention was received, with approval or displeasure carried by the occupant's other behaviour. I recommend keeping the hush distinct from the Narrator's ship-wide white hold.
asks.tree_changes: Attention alone needs a witness-gated acknowledgement with no guaranteed reward. Approval needs a matching campaign state and a control where the deed is seen but disapproved. A coming answer needs a defined follow-up or an honest expiry. If the meaning varies by occupant, each authored use must establish its meaning; the framework does not infer a witness from the effect it just produced.

asks.text: What should you see as you read and dismiss those two letters: one continuous address, a fresh rise for each, or a deliberate sequence of separate performances?
asks.decision: Two letters before the lights have returned
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F2/F3. White priority, real time through pause and returning to the current underlying pattern are settled. Overlapping addresses still need an identity and end condition; a timer-only gesture can finish while someone is still reading or strand white forever.
asks.guess: One continuous white address while any Narrator letter being addressed remains open, then one return. I recommend it because a second white rise from white carries little new information.
asks.tree_changes: A continuous address needs overlapping lifetime ownership and a last-close rule. Separate rises need an observable restart without losing the underlying alarm. A queue needs cancellation and close-order rules. All variants retain the Narrator above the alarm and restore the current underlying state, including any intervening external lamp edit. Reload still restarts gently; it does not acquire mid-gesture persistence through this question.

asks.text: During that predator's silence, what should remain audible from the gods, and what should the sudden quiet mean?
asks.decision: When another creature makes the world go quiet
asks.author: Codex Designer rehearsal 2026-11-10

review.why: Author evidence and wording check only; no independent reviewer run or invented pass.

asks.why_it_matters: F1/F2. Camera listening, both channels shipping together and leaving the cathedral hum's system alone are settled. The predator currently ends biome ambient sounds; it has no agreement with the future AtmosphericBase beds. Simply adding another loop could erase a meaningful survival cue.
asks.guess: The predator cue should stay legible, while the occupants' response has an authored meaning of its own. I recommend comparing a bed that yields briefly with one that continues as an unmistakably separate voice, using existing cathedral behaviour as a fixed neighbour.
asks.tree_changes: Yielding adds a silence-event interaction and exact recovery of AtmosphericBase's own bed. Continuing requires the predator cue to remain understandable alongside it, judged by listening. A god-specific response belongs in the campaign's authored mapping. Nothing here authorises editing the cathedral hum, inferring a current third-party mod list, or turning sound playtest notes into an automated gate.

contradictions.text: Walk/package never-live language is stale. Live runs measured cost failure and proof-induced dark lamps. Later L0/offline implementation events and game infra holds are not an accepted live owner look.

Rank/front supplier found in Rites; nine signatures and 27 readings found in campaign Defs/AtmosphericBase. Search excludes only the exact framework root; identically named neighbour directories remain searched. Authored data is present; active code consumer/subscriber still not found.

Script families accounted for below. Preparation, negative controls and finally blocks exist, but full state restoration, persistent recovery journal, review hold and owner perception coverage are not complete. No build items filed in this rehearsal.

Union allocation can overstep a claimant's group; flasher cache omits membership identity; L8 validation tests primitive label rather than actual visible motion; Coil reconstructs historical steps despite bounded-hitch prose. These are engineering risks, not requests to reduce built scope.

Officiated front can differ from live loudest. Framework orders supplied ranks and uses a fixed/tuned territorial share, not engagement-magnitude share. Wiring must derive intended priority from existing campaign rules; no owner question asks him to repeat those rules.

The DRAFT north star was stopped for live play, later TBD item dropped rather than certified. No evidence located of a later owner live look approving refined bars. Question bank is prospective dialogue; it neither edits nor automates that section.

At x=110+2*i for 14 lamps and fixed z, removing final end lamp as Pick control leaves 13 subjects in seven distinct x/4 blocks; MIN_SPREAD is 8. Local PowerShell arithmetic confirms this conditional bare-site mismatch. No runtime order or actual existing-map selection was measured.

failure_modes: F1: Beautiful motion says nothing true: presences blur together, ordinary drift looks like a change of power, or chosen darkness looks like failed wiring. It may even read as the ship emoting. Sources: design/RimMandrake/atmospheric_base_mod_definition.md; design/validation_walks/RimMandrake/AtmosphericBase.md.

F2: A convincing light demo stands in for the finished mod: sound, Narrator restoration, real campaign consumers or honest witness records are missing while synthetic claims appear complete. Sources: src/RimMandrake/AtmosphericBase/Source/RM_AtmosphericBaseProof.cs:482; design/RimMandrake/atmospheric_base_mod_definition.md.

F3: Borrowing the lighting breaks trust or play: lamps outside intended groups change, external edits/ownership are mishandled, tests leave state behind, or long-running patterns stall the game despite changed-only writes. Sources: src/RimMandrake/AtmosphericBase/Source/RM_AtmosphericCompositor.cs:365; src/RimMandrake/AtmosphericBase/Source/Kernel/RM_PatternWalkers.cs:352; infrastructure/state/ledger/events/FOUNDRY.jsonl:7262.

root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: AtmosphericBase lets other mods speak through a colony's existing lights and ambient sound. The player hands lamps over and can take them back with their own colour restored; animals, plants, worn gear and holograms keep their own light. Away from the Utinni, the handed-over lamps offer beautiful, gentle patterns the player chooses. Aboard an Utinni gravship, the gods choose: two presences hold separate, slowly moving areas, and quieter presences intrude briefly in their own colours. Hue and movement carry identity; real illumination makes their choices matter to colony life. The Narrator commands a reserved white above everything, even an alarm, then returns the lamps to what should be showing underneath. Chosen darkness carries motion; a power failure silences the powered channels. The gods are tenants using the wiring, never feelings of the ship itself. The framework supplies the common patterns, claims and restoration; the campaign supplies their meaning and consequences. Sound shares that language, with the camera as listener. Both channels belong to the finished mod.
